items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] It's alright, Mrs. Brunish, if you want to say something...

ctx.x: Yeah, Emmett Hardy was a good little jazz connet player. So, he used to come up and he used to follow me all over and try to get ideas and all like that for me. And he went out and he went out wonderful. And it's a pity that he had to die so young. He did, yeah. He did, yeah. He did, yeah. He did, yeah. And, uh... Roger. And the Hardy. And the Hardy, yeah. That was it. And Dick, what about the carnival balls?
It's alright, Mrs. Brunish, if you want to say something, dude, you can move up there and you don't have to play.

We used to play at the Outfellas Hall, big balls like the Druids, Masons and all like that, the Fishies Band, you know. Did they play parades too, like carnival? Parades, yeah. Like carnival parades, we used to have five, uh, five, uh, the whole five carnival parades. The other time I was one trumpet player with two bands. And the floats, they used to be led by mules.
